title: Geometric-point criterion for an etale equivalence relation
statement: Let $S,U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ be a morphism, with fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $s$ and $t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose there are morphisms $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{t,U,s}R\to R$ satisfying $je=\Delta_U$, $ji=\mathrm{flip}\circ j$, and $jc=(s\circ\mathrm{pr}_1,t\circ\mathrm{pr}_2)$. Assume that for every algebraically closed field $K$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, $j$ identifies $R(K)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(K)$. Then $j$ is a monomorphism, and for every $S$-scheme $T$ the image of $R(T)$ in $U(T)\times U(T)$ is an equivalence relation. A monomorphism means a map cancellable on the left in every Hom set. Here $V(K)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Spec}K,V)$ and $V(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,V)$.

source.place: Tag 0DT7, lemma-etale-equivalence-relation, specialized from unramified to etale projections.

proof.text: Put $B=U\times_SU$, let $p_1:B\to U$ be the first projection, and put $P=R\times_B R$. The etale hypothesis on $s$ implies that $s$ is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Since $p_1\circ j=s$, the cancellation clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-composition-cancellation] implies that $j$ is unramified, without any hypothesis on $p_1$. Thus its diagonal $d=\Delta_j:R\to P$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. The fibre products and $d$ are given by [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0DT7 (lemma-etale-equivalence-relation), proof, first two sentences (Tags 02GG and 02GE)

proof.text: For any algebraically closed field $K$ and any $K$-point $q$ of $P$ over $S$, write $a,b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to R$ for its two projections. They satisfy $ja=jb$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The hypothesis that $j$ identifies $R(K)$ with an equivalence relation includes injectivity of $R(K)\to U(K)\times U(K)$, so $a=b$. The universal property then gives $q=d\circ a$. Thus every such $q$ lifts through $d$.

Let $z\in P$. Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $\kappa(z)$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The pair consisting of $z$ and the embedding $\kappa(z)\to K$ determines a morphism $q:\operatorname{Spec}K\to P$ whose image is $z$, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. Its composite with $P\to S$ supplies the required $S$-structure on $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Step 2 lifts $q$ through $d$, hence $z$ is in the image of $d$. Therefore $d$ is surjective. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $d$ identifies $R$ with the open subscheme on its image; since that image is all of $P$, $d$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DT7 (lemma-etale-equivalence-relation), proof, surjectivity and isomorphism of the open diagonal; Schemes Tag 01J9

proof.text: To verify the asserted monomorphism in every Hom set, take any scheme $T$ and morphisms $a,b:T\to R$ with $ja=jb$. By [def-pc-fibre-product] they define $h=(a,b):T\to P$. Set $r=d^{-1}\circ h$. Both projections of $d$ are $\mathrm{id}_R$, so $a=r=b$. This proves left cancellation for $j$, including test schemes $T$ with nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 0DT7 (lemma-etale-equivalence-relation), proof, monomorphism conclusion, expanded using the fibre product

proof.text: Fix an $S$-scheme $T$, and define $x\sim y$ for $x,y\in U(T)$ to mean that some $r:T\to R$ has $(sr,tr)=(x,y)$. For each $x$, the map $e\circ x$ witnesses $x\sim x$ by $je=\Delta_U$. If $r$ witnesses $x\sim y$, then $i\circ r$ witnesses $y\sim x$ by $ji=\mathrm{flip}\circ j$. If $r$ witnesses $x\sim y$ and $r\prime$ witnesses $y\sim z$, then $tr=sr\prime$ gives $(r,r\prime):T\to R\times_{t,U,s}R$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], and $c\circ(r,r\prime)$ witnesses $x\sim z$ by the stipulated formula for $jc$. These witnesses are over $S$ because their composites with $j$ have the displayed $S$-valued coordinates. Thus the image is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Left cancellation from step 4 also identifies $R(T)$ with this image.
